answer: Think of the network as a garden where each identity must plant its own time-locked bond: a deposit frozen for weeks, one bond per account, never shared. Anyone who proves two accounts are run by the same operator triggers slashing, and the forfeited bond pays the challenger as a bounty. The velvet glove is the open challenge process; the vertex of the rule is simple — one bond covers exactly one identity. Each fake identity therefore risks a whole bond of its own, so the attacker's cost grows linearly and cannot be amortized.
